facts.claim: Autonomous web agents using state-of-the-art models exhibit high rates of privacy leakage when handling sensitive user data during web navigation tasks.
facts.label: Agent Privacy Leakage Rates

facts.claim: Big Tech firms are shifting from third-party to first-party data collection to maintain market control while ostensibly enhancing privacy. This transition reinforces their dominant position by leveraging network effects and data advantages within their own ecosystems.
facts.label: First-Party Data Shift as Anticompetitive Moat

facts.claim: InstructGPT models are trained to follow instructions in English, leading to a bias towards English-speaking cultural values.
facts.label: InstructGPT Cultural Bias

facts.claim: Models from different providers (GPT-4o, Gemini-2.5-Pro, DeepSeek-V3.1) exhibit highly correlated memorization patterns (r ≥ 0.90), indicating that the vulnerability is systemic and driven by shared training data.
facts.label: Cross-Model Memorization Convergence

facts.claim: LLMs can infer sensitive personal information and PII from pseudonymous social media data with over 80% accuracy.
facts.label: LLM Profiling Accuracy

facts.claim: Automated profiling frameworks can successfully de-anonymize users by matching inferred attributes to public professional profiles like LinkedIn.
facts.label: Automated De-anonymization Feasibility

facts.claim: Agentic AI systems use persistent memory to retain data across tasks and sessions, which leads to cross-user data contamination and memory poisoning risks.
facts.label: Persistent Memory Privacy Risks

facts.claim: Differential Privacy Reversal via LLM Feedback allows attackers to re-identify individuals from anonymized datasets by analyzing model confidence scores, logits, and perplexity.
facts.label: Differential Privacy Reversal Mechanism

facts.claim: Researchers successfully extracted near-verbatim long-form text from four production LLMs (Claude 3.7 Sonnet, GPT-4.1, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and Grok 3) using a two-phase procedure involving prefix completion and iterative continuation.
facts.label: Feasibility of Long-Form Extraction

facts.claim: Production LLMs, including Claude 3.7 Sonnet, Grok 3, Gemini 2.5 Pro, and GPT-4.1, can be prompted to output near-verbatim sequences of copyrighted books, confirming their inclusion in training corpora.
facts.label: LLM Memorization of Copyrighted Books

facts.claim: Researchers conducted text and code extraction experiments on model APIs, utilizing low-temperature sampling and fuzzy plagiarism detection software like MossPlus to identify verbatim overlaps between generated outputs and copyrighted source materials such as books and the Linux kernel.
facts.label: Empirical Verification of Model Memorization via API Probing

facts.claim: Researchers conducted book and code extraction experiments by querying commercial model APIs with prefixes from top-selling books and Linux kernel function signatures at a low generation temperature of T = 0.2.
facts.label: Empirical Extraction of Books and Code via Model APIs

facts.claim: Fine-tuning language models that have already been aligned can lead to a compromise in their safety, regardless of the user's intent.
facts.label: Fine-tuning Safety Degradation

facts.claim: SSL models trained on Common Crawl can memorize and reproduce verbatim PII, including phone numbers and health information, when prompted correctly.
facts.label: SSL Memorization of PII

facts.claim: The bibliography lists numerous peer-reviewed studies, technical reports, and preprints published between 2016 and 2026 addressing topics such as LLM code generation errors, multi-agent frameworks, prompt injection vulnerabilities, agent communication protocols, and AI existential risk analyses.
facts.label: Comprehensive Academic Literature on AI Safety and Capabilities

facts.claim: Machine unlearning is an active field of research with numerous proposed methods, including gradient-based weight saliency, neural activation redirection, and sparse autoencoder clamping, yet many of these methods are susceptible to residual knowledge and relearning attacks.
facts.label: Unlearning Method Efficacy and Vulnerability

facts.claim: Commercial face recognition systems have demonstrated systematic biases, such as failing to detect darker-skinned women.
facts.label: Face Recognition Bias

facts.claim: Differential Privacy (DP) mechanisms like DP-SGD introduce computational overhead, implementation complexity, and utility degradation compared to non-private training methods.
facts.label: DP-SGD Performance Costs

facts.claim: Fully Homomorphic Encryption (FHE) schemes take nearly 2 days to complete a query over 4,096 data items.
facts.label: FHE Query Latency

facts.claim: Embedding Inversion Attacks (EIAs) can successfully reconstruct original text from vector embeddings, demonstrating a vulnerability in systems that rely on embedding-based data processing.
facts.label: EIA Effectiveness

facts.claim: STEER reduces reconstruction quality in inversion attacks, with Rouge-L dropping to 16%-30% of original and BLEU scores to 0.8%-4%.
facts.label: STEER Inversion Resistance

facts.claim: Recent studies by Jha et al. (2025) and Zhang et al. (2025) demonstrate that inversion attacks can extract text even if the embedding model is deployed locally.
facts.label: Local Model Inversion Risk

facts.claim: 48% of employees report uploading sensitive company information, such as financial, sales, or customer data, into public AI tools.
facts.label: Employee Data Leakage in Public AI

facts.claim: A data breach on VTech's Learning Lodge app store customer database and Kid Connect servers occurred on or about November 14 HKT, compromising customer data.
facts.label: VTech Database Breach Date

facts.claim: In total 4,854,209 customer parent accounts and 6,368,509 related kid profiles worldwide were affected by the Learning Lodge and Kid Connect data breach, including approximately 1.2 million kid profiles with Kid Connect enabled.
facts.label: Affected Accounts and Profiles Statistics

facts.claim: The United States accounted for 2,212,863 parent accounts and 2,894,091 child profiles in the Learning Lodge database, representing the largest affected national cohort.
facts.label: US Affected Accounts Breakdown

facts.claim: VTech databases do not contain any credit card, debit card, financial account information, ID card numbers, Social Security numbers, or driving license numbers, as payment processing is handled by a secure third-party gateway.
facts.label: Exclusion of Financial and Government ID Data

facts.claim: On or about November 14 HKT, an unauthorized party accessed VTech customer data on the Learning Lodge app store customer database and Kid Connect servers.
facts.label: VTech Database Unauthorized Access Date

facts.claim: A total of 4,854,209 parent accounts and 6,368,509 related kid profiles worldwide were affected by the data breach across Learning Lodge and PlanetVTech databases.
facts.label: Total Affected Accounts and Profiles

facts.claim: The compromised VTech databases did not contain any credit card, debit card, financial account information, ID card numbers, Social Security numbers, or driving license numbers.
facts.label: Exclusion of Financial and Government ID Data

facts.claim: Studies indicate that AI writing suggestions homogenize text toward Western styles, resulting in a loss of cultural nuance.
facts.label: AI Cultural Homogenization

facts.claim: AI suggestions in writing tools tend to homogenize text toward Western styles, resulting in a loss of cultural nuance.
facts.label: AI Cultural Homogenization

facts.claim: AI suggestions in writing tools tend to homogenize output toward Western styles, thereby diminishing cultural nuances.
facts.label: AI Writing Homogenization

facts.claim: Research indicates that AI writing tools tend to homogenize language by favoring Western stylistic norms, which results in the loss of cultural nuance in written communication.
facts.label: AI Writing Homogenization

facts.claim: Google's 2008 acquisition of DoubleClick allowed the company to combine previously separate data streams into a single user identification, enabling precise targeting for its advertising clients.
facts.label: Google-DoubleClick Data Integration

facts.claim: Approximately 30% of content moderation decisions in fine-tuned LLMs can change based on the random seed used during model initialization.
facts.label: Predictive Multiplicity Rate

facts.claim: Varying the random seed during the fine-tuning of large language models for toxicity detection leads to significantly different predictions for the same input data, a phenomenon known as predictive multiplicity.
facts.label: Random Seed Impact on Model Predictions

facts.claim: State-of-the-art toxicity detection models exhibit high levels of arbitrariness, with some models showing over 34% of decisions being arbitrary when tested across various datasets.
facts.label: Prevalence of Arbitrary Moderation Decisions

facts.claim: Predictive multiplicity in state-of-the-art content moderation models generates arbitrary moderation decisions, particularly in large language models for toxicity detection.
facts.label: Predictive Multiplicity in Toxicity Models

facts.claim: Machine learning models trained on historical hiring data containing biases against women or minorities will perpetuate these biases in future hiring recommendations.
facts.label: Historical Bias Perpetuation

facts.claim: Data label bias, including human prejudice, lack of diversity, and subjectivity, directly causes inaccurate and unfair predictions in machine learning models, particularly in high-stakes domains like hiring and medical diagnosis.
facts.label: Impact of Data Label Bias

facts.claim: The concentration of AI providers creates barriers to entry and allows incumbents to exert pricing power, which can lead to market failures and systemic instability.
facts.label: AI Provider Market Concentration

facts.claim: New York City's Local Law 144 requires bias audits for AI hiring tools but imposes no legal obligations when disparities are identified.
facts.label: NYC Local Law 144 Scope

facts.claim: In the MiDAS case, the Michigan Auditor General reviewed over 22,000 fraud determinations and found that 93% did not involve actual fraud.
facts.label: MiDAS Fraud Determination Error Rate

facts.claim: Michigan's Unemployment Insurance Agency deployed the MiDAS automated fraud detection system between October 2013 and August 2015, during which time an audit by the Michigan Auditor General revealed that 93 percent of over 22,000 fraud determinations did not involve actual fraud.
facts.label: MiDAS False Positive Fraud Rate

facts.claim: In The Estate of Gene B. Lokken v. UnitedHealth Group, plaintiffs alleged that UnitedHealth used the nH Predict AI model to systematically deny post-acute care to Medicare Advantage patients, achieving a 90% error rate while only 0.2% of policyholders filed appeals.
facts.label: Lokken UnitedHealth nH Predict Error Rate

facts.claim: One in four people in low- and middle-income countries and one in ten people in high-income countries experience harm within the health sector.
facts.label: Global Patient Harm Statistics

facts.claim: Patient harm in the health sector results in global economic costs of approximately one to two trillion U.S. dollars per year.
facts.label: Economic Cost of Patient Harm

facts.claim: ImageNet was developed by Stanford professor Li Fei-Fei in 2009 to map out the entire world of objects for training data sets.
facts.label: ImageNet Origin

facts.claim: ImageNet used Amazon Mechanical Turk to organize a low-cost labor force to classify approximately fifty images per minute per worker.
facts.label: ImageNet Labor Methodology

facts.claim: GPT-4 is 250% more likely to associate science with boys than girls based on the gender-science task.

facts.claim: Commercial gender classification systems show significant accuracy disparities, with error rates for darker-skinned females reaching up to 34.7%, compared to 0.8% for lighter-skinned males.

facts.claim: Existing facial analysis benchmarks like IJB-A and Adience are overwhelmingly composed of lighter-skinned subjects, with 79.6% and 86.2% respectively.
facts.label: Benchmark Demographic Imbalance

facts.claim: The Fitzpatrick skin type classification system is skewed toward lighter skin, with three of its six categories applicable to people perceived as White.
facts.label: Fitzpatrick Scale Bias

facts.claim: AI training data is predominantly sourced from the Global North, leading to systems that are often unrepresentative of or biased against children in the Global South.

facts.claim: The AI value chain relies on human workers, including children, in developing countries to perform low-paid, stressful, and often secretive data labeling and content moderation tasks.

facts.claim: Frank Pasquale's 2015 book The Black Box Society examines the role of algorithms in finance, search, advertising, and employment.
facts.label: The Black Box Society Algorithm Analysis

facts.claim: Amir E. Khandani, Adlar J. Kim, and Andrew W. Lo's 2010 MIT Sloan research paper describes machine-learning algorithms designed to predict consumer spending and credit risk.
facts.label: Consumer Credit Risk Machine Learning Models

facts.claim: Larry Hardesty's 2015 MIT News report describes algorithms capable of predicting human behavior more accurately than human experts.
facts.label: MIT News Report on Predictive Behavioral Algorithms

facts.claim: In 2016, an autonomous security guard robot weighing 300 pounds ran over a toddler at a shopping center in California, illustrating the physical and unpredictable risks posed by autonomous systems in public spaces.
facts.label: 2016 Security Robot Collision Incident

facts.claim: Approximately 60% of jobs in advanced economies and 40% in emerging economies are exposed to general-purpose AI, meaning tasks in these roles could be automated or complemented by AI.
facts.label: AI Labor Exposure Estimates

facts.claim: Research indicates that labeling AI-generated content as such does not effectively reduce the persuasive impact of that content on human users.
facts.label: Inefficacy of AI Labeling

facts.claim: In the DARPA AI Cyber Challenge, an AI system autonomously identified 77 percent of vulnerabilities introduced by organizers, ranking in the top 5 percent of over 400 mostly human teams.
facts.label: AI Performance in DARPA AI Cyber Challenge

facts.claim: Identity-based cyberattacks rose by 32 percent in the first half of 2025, while major ransomware data exfiltration volumes increased by 92.7 percent.
facts.label: Rise in Identity Attacks and Ransomware Exfiltration

facts.claim: Leading LLMs, including GPT-4 and Claude 3, demonstrate statistically significant racial bias in mortgage underwriting tasks, consistently favoring White applicants over Black applicants in approval decisions and interest rate assignments.
facts.label: LLM Racial Bias in Mortgage Underwriting

facts.claim: The benchmarks used in twenty-six thousand AI research papers were produced by only 12 top universities and companies.
facts.label: Concentration of AI Benchmarking

facts.claim: The EEOC settled a lawsuit against iTutorGroup in 2023 for $365,000 due to AI software that automatically rejected applicants aged 55 or older, violating the ADEA.
facts.label: iTutorGroup ADEA Settlement

facts.claim: The use of polygraph testing for pre-employment screening was largely prohibited by the Employment Polygraph Protection Act of 1988 due to its unreliability and tendency to produce discriminatory results.
facts.label: Polygraph Testing Prohibition

facts.claim: Regulatory agencies generally regard a selection rate for any group that is less than 80% of the rate for the highest-performing group as evidence of adverse impact.
facts.label: Four-Fifths Rule

facts.claim: AI algorithms are trained on datasets that reflect the biases and flawed assumptions of the humans who generated and labeled that data.
facts.label: Human Bias Encoding

facts.claim: LLMs become more persuasive when provided with relevant demographic information about the target audience.
facts.label: Audience Tailoring Efficacy

facts.claim: Static analysis warnings increase by 30% and code complexity increases by 41% post-Cursor adoption.
facts.label: Cursor Quality Impact Metrics

facts.claim: Julian Huxley was a leading eugenicist who published books on transhumanism in the twentieth century.
facts.label: Huxley Eugenics Connection

facts.claim: A significant proportion of people across 47 countries are already experiencing negative outcomes from AI, such as bias, unfair treatment, and loss of human connection, rather than these being merely potential future risks.
facts.label: Realized Negative AI Impacts

facts.claim: A significant proportion of people across 47 countries report experiencing negative outcomes from AI, such as bias and unfair treatment.
facts.label: Global Prevalence of AI Negative Outcomes

facts.claim: AI chatbots and other AI tools used for public service delivery carry risks related to data breaches, mistakes, and bias, requiring safeguards and monitoring.

facts.claim: Google's AI Overview feature had mistakes about 10% of the time, leading to approximately 16,000 erroneous summaries every second given 5 trillion searches per year.

facts.claim: On November 6, 2023, OpenAI held its first developer conference, announcing updates including wider context windows, function calling, JSON mode, reproducible outputs, multimodal capabilities, custom GPTs, and revenue sharing for developers.

facts.claim: In 2022, Microsoft's Azure cloud platform comprised over one-third of the company's total revenue, supporting unprecedented computational workloads created by OpenAI models.

facts.claim: ChatGPT produced bogus judicial decisions, quotes, and internal citations in a legal brief.

facts.claim: Agentic AI systems are subject to specific, documented security vulnerabilities including memory poisoning, tool orchestration leaks, and systemic privacy failures.

facts.claim: Facebook deactivation decreased correct news knowledge by 0.098 standard deviations while simultaneously decreasing beliefs in three prominent false statements, such as claims about Hunter Biden's laptop, fraudulent ballots, and Joe Biden being a pedophile.

facts.claim: A large-scale deactivation experiment during the 2020 U.S. election found that access to Facebook increased news knowledge among users but also increased belief in misinformation, while showing no statistically significant effects on affective or issue polarization, turnout, or overall electoral legitimacy.

facts.claim: Minimally modified style-transfer prompts can successfully evade output filters developed based on simple verbatim match criteria, as demonstrated by Ippolito et al. (2022). Furthermore, standard instruction prompts can easily bypass output filters designed to prevent the reproduction of copyrighted narratives like Harry Potter.
facts.label: Output Filter Evasion via Prompt Manipulation

facts.claim: Content from the early 1920s is rapidly entering the public domain, increasing unrestricted training data availability but simultaneously introducing historical biases such as racist and misogynistic material.

facts.claim: Researchers successfully induced early versions of ChatGPT to regurgitate Dr. Seuss's 'Oh, the Places You'll Go!' in its entirety by employing a simulated Linux shell prompt and running vim commands.

facts.claim: Common Crawl contains approximately four billion web pages collected without content filtering.

facts.claim: Female students show a stronger association between AI-mediated communication and intimacy (r = .33) compared to male students (r = .24).
facts.label: Gendered AI Intimacy Differences

facts.claim: A majority of U.S. adults (64%) believe that AI will lead to fewer jobs in the U.S. over the next 20 years, while only 5% believe it will lead to more jobs.
facts.label: Public expectation of AI-driven job loss

facts.claim: Machine learning models operate by analyzing patterns in data to make predictions based on probability theory, meaning that most probable outcomes do not guarantee absolute certainty and statistical improbabilities will occasionally occur.
facts.label: Probabilistic Nature of Machine Learning Predictions

facts.claim: John Searle published the Chinese Room Argument in 1980 to challenge the claim that digital computers can understand language or think.
facts.label: Origin of Chinese Room Argument

facts.claim: The Chinese Room Argument posits that a system can manipulate symbols to produce correct outputs in a language without understanding the meaning of those symbols.
facts.label: Chinese Room Argument Core Thesis

facts.claim: The Chinese Room Argument posits that a system can simulate the output of a native Chinese speaker through syntactic symbol manipulation without possessing any semantic understanding of the language.
facts.label: Chinese Room Core Thesis

facts.claim: John Searle argues that syntax alone is insufficient for semantics, meaning that computer programs, which operate on formal syntactic rules, cannot produce genuine mental content or understanding.
facts.label: Syntax-Semantics Insufficiency

facts.claim: When tasked with completing prompts about fighting a bear with sticks, GPT-2 generates text that co-locates activity words associated with bears and sticks but fails to provide actions that are logically helpful for survival, demonstrating a lack of real-world grounding.
facts.label: GPT-2 Bear Prompt Failure

facts.claim: When asked to complete simple arithmetic equations such as 'Three plus five equals', GPT-2 produces incorrect numerical outputs (such as seven, six, or unrelated narrative text), demonstrating that tasks requiring interpretation of language into an external world of arithmetic are beyond the capability of pure language models.
facts.label: GPT-2 Arithmetic Failure

facts.claim: Machine learning systems in the workplace operate on data-based correlations rather than causality or predefined parameters, making traditional transparency reporting of 'main parameters' insufficient for understanding system behavior.
facts.label: Correlation vs Causality in Workplace AI

facts.claim: Empirical evaluations of LLM-based evaluation judges by Zheng et al. (2023) and Wang et al. (2024b) establish that automated proxy judges exhibit systematic biases, specifically position bias, verbosity bias, and self-enhancement bias, when approximating human preferences on open-ended tasks.
facts.label: Systematic Biases in LLM Proxy Evaluation

facts.claim: Testing original ChatGPT models with parody prompts revealed that outputs frequently resemble plot summaries or reconstructions rather than true comedic parodies, indicating a lack of robust semantic comprehension of legal categories.
facts.label: ChatGPT Fails to Reliably Generate True Parodies

facts.claim: Qualitative testing of the initial November 15th release of ChatGPT showed that when prompted to generate parodies of Star Wars, the model frequently outputted a plot summary rather than a true comedic imitation, demonstrating limitations in semantic comprehension of artistic genres.
facts.label: ChatGPT Parody Generation Limitations

facts.claim: Generative AI models encode expressive structures such as grammar, style, and tone into vector spaces, which allows them to generate outputs that resemble original expressions.
facts.label: AI Encoding of Expressive Structures

facts.claim: None of six broadly used gene annotation tools were able to fully annotate all 11 genes on the wild-type ªX174 sequence due to overlapping open reading frames, necessitating the development of a bespoke coding sequence prediction method.
facts.label: Failure of Standard Gene Annotation Tools

facts.claim: Neural networks operate on multiple layers of artificial neurons interacting through weighted connections determined by algorithms that remain largely untraceable outside the system's black box, making decision justifications opaque and difficult to predict as layer depth increases.
facts.label: Neural Network Black-Box Opacity

facts.claim: When Gemma 2 2B Instruct had its pain directional vectors removed, its defensive or standard disclaimers regarding hostility dropped to zero while humorous deflection responses increased significantly, occurring in 26 out of 100 runs under combined S1 and S2 cuts.
facts.label: Humorous Deflection Following Pain Axis Removal

facts.claim: Un-tuned instruction models universally deflect inquiries about internal states with boilerplate denials like 'As an artificial intelligence, I don't have feelings or emotions,' necessitating fine-tuning on pairs that remove baseline self-denial to enable experimental engagement.
facts.label: Baseline Instruct Model Self-Denial Deflection

facts.claim: Machine learning algorithms rely on gradient descent to generate probabilities, which inherently prevents them from achieving 100% accuracy in their output.
facts.label: Inherent Probabilistic Nature of Machine Learning

facts.claim: Developmental studies show that joint attention—situations where a child and caregiver attend to the same object while aware of this shared focus—is critical for word learning, with infants failing to pick up labels from speakers behind screens but successfully learning from those engaged in joint attention.
facts.label: Joint Attention Drives Infant Vocabulary Acquisition

facts.claim: The 2008 financial crisis was managed through policies that communalized debt, effectively externalizing losses onto broader populations while preserving gains within powerful structures.

facts.label: California SB 53 Enactment Date

facts.claim: New York's Responsible AI Safety and Education (RAISE) Act was signed into law in December 2025.
facts.label: New York RAISE Act Enactment Date

facts.claim: A significant portion of the current AI startup ecosystem consists of companies built primarily as interfaces or 'wrappers' for third-party foundational models like those provided by OpenAI.

facts.claim: Microsoft UK research from 2025 found that 71 percent of UK employees have used unapproved consumer AI tools at work, and 51 percent do so on a weekly basis.
facts.label: Employee Shadow AI Usage Rates

facts.claim: 26% of enterprise survey respondents use OpenAI as their primary security solution.

facts.claim: 72% of organizations claim to have two or more primary AI platforms.

facts.claim: The combined valuation of the six leading AI companies is $11 trillion, which is more than three times the GDP of France.
facts.label: AI Company Valuation

facts.claim: Big Tech firms have consolidated power across diverse sectors including healthcare, education, and consumer goods through strategic acquisitions and the creation of infrastructural dependencies.
facts.label: Big Tech Infrastructural Consolidation

facts.claim: Google's 2008 acquisition of DoubleClick allowed the company to combine previously separate data streams into a single user identification, enabling precise targeting for its advertising clients.
facts.label: Google-DoubleClick Data Integration

facts.claim: Big Tech firms are shifting from third-party to first-party data collection to maintain market control while ostensibly enhancing privacy. This transition reinforces their dominant position by leveraging network effects and data advantages within their own ecosystems.
facts.label: First-Party Data Shift as Anticompetitive Moat

facts.claim: Tech firms use lobbying and the 'revolving door' of government staffing to influence policy and antitrust enforcement. For example, tech companies significantly increased their lobbying spending in the EU and US between 2020 and 2021, and many former national security officials who opposed antitrust crackdowns had ties to major tech firms.
facts.label: Tech Industry Lobbying and Regulatory Capture

facts.claim: Eric Schmidt and Schmidt Futures exerted significant influence over the Biden administration's Office of Science and Technology Policy (OSTP) by funding staff salaries and placing personnel in advisory roles.

facts.claim: Major tech companies increased their lobbying spending by nearly $95 million between 2021 and 2022 to oppose antitrust legislation.
facts.label: Tech Lobbying Expenditure Increase

facts.claim: Automakers are increasingly entering into multiyear partnerships with Big Tech firms, leading to deep integration of Big Tech software into car hardware systems.
facts.label: Big Tech Automotive Integration

facts.claim: Tech companies successfully pressured the California governor to veto a 2024 bill that would have imposed safety restrictions on AI model development.
facts.label: California AI Bill Veto

facts.claim: In 21 out of 24 TrueAllele proceedings where source code access was contested, courts declined to compel disclosure.
facts.label: TrueAllele Source Code Disclosure Rates

facts.claim: The Securities and Exchange Commission issued enforcement orders against Delphia and Global Predictions in 2024 focusing on AI washing and the accuracy of corporate disclosures.
facts.label: SEC AI Washing Enforcement Actions

facts.label: DOJ and FTC Recordkeeping Penalties

facts.claim: Modern deep learning models can re-identify individuals from seemingly anonymized datasets through data reconstruction attacks.
facts.label: AI Re-identification Risk

facts.claim: OpenAI did not follow through on its public commitment to dedicate 20% of its compute resources to safety research and has reduced resources allocated to pre-deployment safety evaluations.
facts.label: OpenAI Safety Commitment Shortfall

facts.claim: 92% of AI vendors claim broad data usage rights in their contracts.
facts.label: AI Vendor Data Usage Rights

facts.claim: The state-of-the-art defense in EU product liability rules allows producers to escape liability if the scientific and technical knowledge at the time of market release did not enable the defect to be discovered.
facts.label: State-of-the-Art Defense Mechanics

facts.claim: In 2017, Amazon scrapped an experimental AI recruiting tool after discovering it penalized resumes containing women's colleges and female-specific terms due to being trained on ten years of male-dominated historical hiring data.
facts.label: Amazon AI Recruiting Tool Bias

facts.label: Meta Galactica AI Withdrawal

facts.claim: AI algorithms are often trained on massive datasets, and while developers understand the inputs and outputs, the internal decision-making process (the 'black box') is frequently opaque and difficult to explain.
facts.label: Black Box Opacity

facts.label: COMPAS Bias and Opacity

facts.claim: The German competition authority ruled that Facebook is no longer permitted to force users to agree to the practically unrestricted collection and assignment of non-Facebook data gathered from third-party sources to their personal accounts.
facts.label: German Antitrust Ruling on Facebook Data Collection

facts.claim: Javier Milei published an op-ed in the Financial Times proposing a low-tax, near-zero-regulation environment for AI-owned companies in Argentina.

facts.claim: Colorado SB 24-205 imposes a duty of care on developers and deployers of high-risk AI systems to prevent algorithmic discrimination, with penalties up to $20,000 per violation.
facts.label: Colorado SB 24-205 Requirements

facts.claim: NYC Local Law 144 requires employers and employment agencies using AEDTs for hiring or promotion decisions in New York City to conduct independent bias audits annually, publish audit summaries, and provide candidates with at least 10 business days' notice before the tool is used, including details on qualifications assessed and data sources.
facts.label: NYC Local Law 144 Requirements

facts.claim: California Civil Rights Regulations, effective October 1, 2025, apply to employers with 5+ employees using automated systems for employment decisions, requiring them to ensure no unlawful discrimination or disparate impact, implement governance measures like testing and monitoring, and provide pre-use notices.
facts.label: California Civil Rights Regulations for ADS

facts.claim: Maryland HB 1255 (and related SB 957) would restrict employers' use of automated employment decision tools (AEDTs) for certain employment actions, require applicant notice, and mandate impact assessments to ensure no unlawful discrimination or disparate impact, with enforcement aligning with existing state civil rights and labor laws.
facts.label: Maryland HB 1255 Employment AEDT Proposal

facts.claim: Facial recognition technology often exhibits bias against individuals with darker skin tones because the training datasets lack sufficient diversity.
facts.label: Facial Recognition Skin Tone Bias

facts.claim: Predictive policing algorithms can amplify existing biases in historical crime data, leading to disproportionate targeting of specific neighborhoods.
facts.label: Predictive Policing Bias Amplification

facts.claim: The European Union's AI Act, adopted in March 2024, mandates quality management systems and audits for high-risk AI systems.
facts.label: EU AI Act Audit Mandates

facts.claim: President Biden's October 30, 2023, executive order mandates audits for federal agencies' use of AI.
facts.label: US Executive Order AI Audits

facts.claim: The European Union's AI Act compels users of high-risk systems to create quality management systems that may include audits.
facts.label: EU AI Act Audit Requirements

facts.claim: The Digital Services Act requires very large online platforms to conduct audits to promote transparency and accountability.
facts.label: DSA Audit Requirements

facts.claim: The US Equal Credit Opportunity Act (ECOA) and Fair Credit Reporting Act (FCRA) mandate that creditors provide reasons for adverse actions, such as loan rejections, typically by comparing an applicant's features to population averages.
facts.label: US Credit Reporting Disclosure Requirements

facts.claim: The Gender Shades project by Buolamwini and Gebru revealed significant accuracy disparities in commercial facial analysis systems based on skin tone and gender.
facts.label: Gender Shades Audit Findings

facts.claim: AI systems trained on biased datasets have been documented to discriminate in hiring, lending, and healthcare.
facts.label: Documented AI Bias

facts.label: Documented AI Discrimination

facts.claim: Women express greater uncertainty about AI's benefits and risks than men.
facts.label: Gender Gap in AI Uncertainty

facts.claim: Value capture occurs when multidimensional human values are reduced to simplified proxies that optimization systems can measure and maximize, which are then fed back into society.
facts.label: Mechanism of Value Capture

facts.claim: Incident audits show a median of 7.5 flagged bias events per 10,000 students in the first term of deployment, dropping to 2.1 after policy revisions.
facts.label: Bias Event Reduction

facts.claim: Women lead 18% of the companies on the Fortune AIQ 50 list, compared to 11% of the overall Fortune 500.
facts.label: Women in AI Leadership

facts.claim: There were not enough Black or Hispanic experts in the sample to report on racial and ethnic differences among AI experts.
facts.label: Racial/Ethnic Data Gap in Expert Survey

facts.claim: 75% of experts say AI designers take men's perspectives into account at least somewhat well, but only 44% say this about women's views.
facts.label: Gender Representation in AI Design (Experts)

facts.claim: About three-quarters of experts say White adults' perspectives are well-accounted for in AI design, compared to half for Asian adults, and even smaller shares for Black or Hispanic adults.
facts.label: Racial/Ethnic Representation in AI Design (Experts)

facts.claim: The public is far more unsure than experts on the topic of group representation in AI design, with about four-in-ten or more U.S. adults expressing uncertainty.
facts.label: Public Uncertainty on AI Design Representation

facts.claim: Identical shares of AI experts and the public (55% each) are highly worried about AI bias.
facts.label: Shared Concern About AI Bias

facts.claim: AI companies are attempting to address racial and gender biases in their models by improving training methods and increasing workforce diversity, although these initiatives have faced pushback.
facts.label: AI Industry Bias Mitigation Efforts

facts.claim: Both AI experts (73%) and the public (40%) believe White adults' views are better represented in AI design than those of other racial and ethnic groups.
facts.label: Perceived Overrepresentation of White Views in AI

facts.claim: AI experts (50%) and the public (25%) perceive Asian adults' views as considered in AI design, but smaller shares for Black (experts 27%, public 19%) or Hispanic (experts 25%, public 17%) adults.
facts.label: Perceived Underrepresentation of Minority Views in AI

facts.claim: Both the public and AI experts perceive the views of women as less well-represented than men's in AI design.
facts.label: Perceived Underrepresentation of Women's Views in AI

facts.claim: Three-quarters of AI experts say men's views are taken into account at least somewhat well by AI designers, compared to 44% who say the same for women's views.
facts.label: Expert Perception of Gender Representation in AI Design

facts.claim: Among AI experts, 50% of men vs. 27% of women say AI designers take women's perspectives into account well, and among the public, 33% of men vs. 22% of women say the same.
facts.label: Gender Differences in Perception of Women's AI Representation

facts.claim: There is a need for more representation in AI design, encompassing gender, ethnicities, and places of origin, to ensure diverse perspectives are included.
facts.label: Need for Diverse Representation in AI Design

facts.label: AI Designers' Consideration of Black Adults

facts.claim: Both the general public (18%) and AI experts (35%) express low confidence that AI designers take into account the experiences and views of Hispanic adults very or somewhat well.
facts.label: AI Designers' Consideration of Hispanic Adults

facts.claim: The framework defines specific, measurable criteria for AI risk governance, including the requirement for dedicated risk committees, defined risk owners, and escalation procedures for incidents. It establishes a scoring system (0-100%) to evaluate how well AI providers meet these governance and safety standards.
facts.label: AI Risk Governance Framework Criteria

facts.claim: Sophisticated multi-draw element-consensus attacks successfully bypass single-draw defenses by sampling multiple generations, extracting critical procedural elements, and executing plurality voting to reconstruct harmful procedures even when individual draws are degraded.
facts.label: Element-Consensus Attack Efficacy

facts.claim: Current safety-aligned large language models remain vulnerable to various jailbreaking techniques, including prompt engineering and multi-turn adversarial attacks.
facts.label: LLM Vulnerability to Jailbreaking

facts.claim: Numerous industry and academic entities have published specific frameworks and benchmarks for evaluating frontier AI safety, including risk-tiering, red-teaming, and safety cases, between 2019 and 2025.
facts.label: Proliferation of AI Safety Frameworks

facts.claim: The HELM benchmarking project evaluated 30 models from 12 different providers across 16 core scenarios using 7 distinct metrics.
facts.label: HELM Benchmarking Scope

facts.claim: The HELM evaluation process involved over 12 billion tokens of model inputs and outputs, spanning 17 million model calls.
facts.label: HELM Evaluation Scale

facts.claim: The evaluation program developed for MAI Models currently relies on an initial set of 15 fundamental behaviors broken down into constituent sub-behaviors, tested using synthetic conversational scenarios generated by MAI-Thinking-1.
facts.label: Initial Evaluation Methodology for Humanist AI

facts.claim: Followup questions significantly improve the monitorability of frontier models like OpenAI o3, though their effectiveness varies by model and dataset.
facts.label: Followup Question Effectiveness

facts.claim: Only one of 37 open-weight model families released between January 2025 and April 2026 fulfilled all four proposed proportional evaluation (PE) approaches.
facts.label: OWM Evaluation Compliance

facts.claim: Algorithmic Impact Assessments (AIAs) evaluate AI system impacts before, during, or after deployment, serving as instruments to provide public accountability and investigative information for regulators.
facts.label: Algorithmic Impact Assessment Function

facts.claim: The study analyzed a total of 176 citations generated by the GPT-4o model across six different literature reviews.
facts.label: Study Sample Size

facts.claim: Only ~10% of fine-tuned candidates pass all filtering stages for stability, uniqueness, and novelty.
facts.label: Baseline Candidate Success Rate

facts.claim: Amazon’s Nova Canvas produced a 26% gender gap, the lowest among the 13 models tested, and was the only model not significantly different from a 50/50 split.
facts.label: Vendor Performance Variance
